chapter_note: The chapter is largely dominated by a systematic cosmological teaching about how the Living Spirit uses three “garments” (wind/water/fire) to discharge and then confine three dark “vessels” (water/darkness/fire), expressed through extended medical and birth analogies and a timed process. The second-half ‘twelve deeds’ enumeration is mostly cosmological, but shows editorial fatigue: explicit institutional/present-world anchoring appears (notably the fasting line; and an ‘apostles’ paragraph), and several paragraphs retain dialogue-attribution seams.

paragraphs.core_text: Tell us, our master, and instruct us about these three vessels that [ ... ] and were discharged from above, and how they were discharged and separated from all the rulers who are arranged in the heavens. For it is a necessity for us to know the manner in which the three vessels have been discharged, while the rulers were flourishing in their body.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the dialogue frame formula (“Once again the disciples questioned the enlightener, saying to him:”). Kept the substantive cosmological question (request for the mechanism of discharge/separation of the three vessels from the heavenly rulers).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core topic is introduced as a structural cosmological problem (three vessels; discharge from above; separation from rulers), but the disciples→enlightener Q&A container is later framing.

paragraphs.core_text: when these vessels were discharged, they were discharged in [ ... ] slaughter, but those [ ... ] these vessels from them.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue-attribution and audience-address layer (“Then the enlightener speaks to his disciples: Happen you know, my beloved ones, that …”).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying line continues the causal/mechanical description of discharge; the address (“my beloved ones”) and speaker tag are later dialogue-frame voice.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.107⟩
They are like the form of a man who has fallen into a purulent sickness. Other wounds and diseases are in his body, and even bile and other poisons are in his inner limbs. He achieves good health by a wise doctor, who gives him one remedy to drink that causes his purulent sickness to break out above, and gives him another medicine to drink that causes his sickness to discharge below, and he gives him yet another medicine to drink that cures his wounds for him [ ... ] calmly and silently.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, process-oriented correspondential analogy (illness/poisons ↔ hidden vessels; discharge above/below) without institutional pointing.

paragraphs.core_text: Through the skill of a wise doctor, with his effective medicines to consume that take away all sicknesses in this manner and dissolve all magic, the doctors shall [ ... ] they work cures through the aroma of the medicine, other wounds [ ... ] what is hidden, they at last tear them out from [ ... ] manifested above and below [ ... through] the aroma of edible medicines that were placed upon them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continuation of the technical healing/discharge model (hidden→manifest; above/below), maintaining the cosmological-analogical register rather than exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: This is also what these vessels of water, of darkness and of fire are like, which are hidden in the body of all the rulers above; while the Living Spirit is like the wise doctor. These three healing drugs are the three garments that the Living Spirit assumes upon his body: of wind, of water, and of fire. Through them he has set in order the things below. For by those three garments he has been displayed to the rulers who are above, with hard-heartedness, with shaking and fear, with derangement; from them he discharged the three vessels, those of water, of darkness and of fire.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Classic substrate mapping: cosmic beings/processes described by stable correspondential equivalences (vessels↔illness; garments↔drugs) and mechanical effects (fear/derangement leading to discharge).

paragraphs.core_text: The case of these vessels is just like a child who is in his mother's womb and is swathed by seven garments. The first is the marrow, the second is the bones, the third is the tendons, the fourth is the flesh, the fifth the veins, the sixth the blood, the seventh the skin of the body that covers him. The other garment also [ ... / ... in the womb of his mother. His mother also is just like] this child. The marrow and the bones, the sinews and flesh, the veins and blood and skin, together with the garment that she wears and the linen that swathes her, total nine. Together with the nine of the child, these and the others, they shall complete and make eighteen garments. Now, you shall find the soul of this child is entwined within all these.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered anatomical layering (7/9/18) is a strong substrate marker: systematic degree-structure and containment imagery used to explain cosmic containment/discharge.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.108⟩
And look see: When the smell of the action of the demon, which brings about the stench of birth, will reveal the child; immediately [ ... ] shall [ ... ] all [these things] and it emerges from a crack that has become visible, while no tear nor wound occurs in the body of the child. In the same way as this child opens up the womb of his mother, so is it also with these vessels of water, of darkness and of fire. The actions that open up his mother to the child, and she shakes him out and reveals him; these are the three living garments that the Living Spirit assumed on his body.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Correspondential birth/discharge mechanism (no wound; emergence through a ‘crack’) mapped directly onto the three vessels/three garments, without contemporary-world targets.

paragraphs.core_text: For by the aspect of the garment of water [ ... / ... ] from the rulers; he moved [ ... ] they are the poison and death with which their veins and entrails are filled.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmos→cosmos description: a specific garment-aspect causes extraction of ‘poison and death’ from rulers’ bodies (internal physiological-cosmic register).

paragraphs.core_text: By the aspect of the garment of wind, in which he was revealed [ ... ] he has swept away and erased the entire destructive shadow and dirt, discharged it down to the earth. Afterwards he swept it out and confined it in the vessel of darkness that surrounds the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Process sequence (reveal→sweep/discharge→sweep again→confine) articulated in cosmic geography (earth; surrounding vessel).

paragraphs.core_text: Also, by the garment of living fire, through its splendour and vigour, he discharged the fire of the darkness from all the rulers and threw it down upon this earth. He swept it another time from the earth and confined it in the vessel that surrounds all the worlds, and they call it the wall of great fire.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic parallel to ¶8–9 (water/wind/fire operations). The ‘wall of great fire’ is cosmological architecture, not institutional pointing.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, those three garments, through which he established these three things, he did not peel them off all at once; but he stripped them off one by one at the appropriate time [ ... ] down to the earth [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Temporal governance (‘one by one at the appropriate time’) is characteristic of the substrate’s mechanical ‘how it works’ voice.

paragraphs.core_text: In this way the universe of the [ ... ... ] his vessels [ ... ] these vessels like [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fragmentary but continues the impersonal, cosmological explication; no frame or institutional language.

paragraphs.core_text: The use of the matter, and the management of these vessels that were swept out and discharged from above to earth, have brought an advantage and benefit of twelve great deeds. Afterwards, they were swept from the earth and pushed outside to the edges of the worlds and to the {extremity}.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue continuation and attribution (“Furthermore, he continued. He says to his disciples:”).
paragraphs.temporal_note: The ‘twelve deeds’ scheme is cosmological-instructional, but the paragraph is introduced by an explicit editorial speech-attribution seam.

paragraphs.core_text: The first deed is this: So that evil-doing does not increase in the universe, neither in the creations nor in the trees [ ... it has set i]tself up in three things.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic-ecological consequence framing (universe/creations/trees) consistent with Manichaean cosmology; still not institutional discipline.

paragraphs.core_text: The [first is / ...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Lacuna fragment within the enumerated cosmological ‘deeds’ sequence; no independent late markers.

paragraphs.core_text: For, if it were so, if [the vessel of water] had not been swept down from above, but rather the waters existing up till now in the rulers above [ ... / ... the] torrents that would flow [ ... ] and the droplets that would [ ... ] down, so lust would have sprouted [ ... i]n the trees and in the fruits as well as all flesh [ ... ] down
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the editorial/application lead-in and self-referential address (“The second is error [ ... ... ] Indeed, about this I have spoken to you as I [ ... ]”). Removed the later pivot into present-world/saint language beginning with the ‘today … you could not find a single person … a saint …’ material.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core portion stays within the cosmic mechanism (upper waters→torrents/droplets→lust in trees/fruits/flesh). The removed tail points into contemporary moral/social evaluation (‘today… saint’), a cosmos→editorial-world mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: Not only this, but if the vessel of darkness had not been swept out and thrown down to the earth, nor swept from the earth and cast outside the region of the worlds into this pit; again the drops of darkness, which will drip down from it, and the torrents that will continue to flow down from above to the earth and assume the trees and all flesh, would have multiplied,
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the present-anchored comparative application (‘the forgetfulness that is in a thousand people today…’) and the following anthropological conclusion fragment.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Old layer is the cosmological hydraulics of Darkness (drips/torrents; trees/flesh; pit at the world’s edge). The ‘today’ scaling to contemporary people is application voice.

paragraphs.core_text: Furthermore, if the fire were in the rulers of the worlds of the heavens until today, and had not been swept out and cast down to the earth, and swept from the earth and shut up inside the vessel of fire that surrounds the worlds; [ ... ] this fire [ ... ... ] above through the torrent [ ... the torrent ... ] below;
paragraphs.temporal_note: Despite the temporal phrase ‘until today’, the paragraph remains within the cosmic containment logic (fire vessel; surrounding worlds; torrent imagery) and does not pivot to institutional practice.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.110⟩
and the dark fire would have multiplied in the tree and in fruit and in all flesh. The power of the fire that is now in a thousand people, you would have found it occurring in a single person today.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the explicit institutional/pastoral consequence: “You would not have found a single person embracing the fast in the universe.”
paragraphs.temporal_note: First two sentences continue the cosmological-physiological escalation pattern (fire in flesh/fruit; quantitative comparison). The fasting line is an institutional discipline application, i.e., editorial use of the teaching.
Meta-teaching address (“Behold, I have taught you…”) functions as a rhetorical transition/closure rather than substrate exposition; it does not advance the cosmic mapping itself.

paragraphs.core_text: The second deed: Al[l] the heavens [ ... / ... ] of the sediment and the pollution [ ... ... ] so that [ ... / ... ] surpasses in them [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmological purification of heavens/firmaments (sediment/pollution) continues the ‘advantages’ list in system-internal terms.

paragraphs.core_text: [The third]: The heavens and the firmaments [ ... / ... b]urden [ ... ] relieved from the weight-carriers [ ... ] and it ceased being heavy. This rich one [ ... ... ] above.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mechanical relief of cosmic structures (‘weight-carriers’) is characteristic of the architectural cosmology layer.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth: That they might purify and cleanse their dwelling places [ ... / ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: System-internal cleansing of heavenly ‘dwelling places’; no institutional identification.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth: Because the greatness and the richness that dwells in these ships, as it [ ... ] you might find them living in these ships, purified and holy.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic ‘ships’ (sun/moon vehicles) as habitats of light-richness is a standard cosmological register.

paragraphs.core_text: The sixth: That you might find the mixed, incomplete, and unconfined temples above at rest and purified; since rest will reach them and pass through them and purify them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: ‘Temples above’ functions as a celestial-architectural term here (qualified by ‘above’, ‘mixed/incomplete/unconfined’), not a polemic about earthly cult sites.

paragraphs.core_text: The seventh: [ ... ] nature alone of the vessels, which will advance and extend to their places and sites [ ... / ... ] in [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Processual description of vessels reaching their cosmic ‘places and sites’ stays inside the system.

paragraphs.core_text: The eighth: That great enclosures and walls would be made, and confine everything.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic containment architecture (‘enclosures and walls’) is a substrate-like explanatory motif.
Explicit institutional marker (“apostles”) signals a later community/church layer grafted into the ‘deeds’ list (cosmos→community agents).

paragraphs.core_text: The tenth deed: That they would become releasers and purifiers of everything at the end of the universe like the fire [ ... / ... ] burns [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eschatological cosmology (‘end of the universe’; purifying fire) stated in impersonal system terms.

paragraphs.core_text: The eleventh deed: [ ... ] will make a crossing [ ... ] and the entire ruling-power [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fragmentary but framed as end-time cosmic transition (‘crossing’; ‘ruling-power’) rather than institutional instruction.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.111⟩
to the outer land, for they were not envious of this [ ... ] a man who is richer than them; because the aeons of light are outside [ ... ] the place [ ... ] of peace, the place of honour and grace, the place where the joy of the householders who dwell in it shall never pass away nor recede.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic geography of the ‘outer land’ and ‘aeons of light’ with enumerated qualitative states (peace/honour/grace) is system-internal and non-citational.

paragraphs.core_text: The twelfth: That you might find all the deeds of loss hidden from the aeons of light, because of the wall of fire that surrounds the entire building; and these unclean things are displayed (only) in its [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Wall-of-fire containment and concealment from the aeons of Light: classic cosmic-architectural mechanism.

paragraphs.core_text: There was a need for these twelve great deeds because the vessels that were discharged and swept out from the firmaments to the earth, and were also swept from the earth to the {extr[emity) ... / ... ] the three words of life watch over them that [ ... / ... ar]e set over them in great power [ ... ] that they might watch over them at the last time; because of this, they are firmly set thus in these fetters, in the way that I have told you.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summative cosmological rationale (discharge→sweep→extremity; guarding ‘three words of life’; fetters) remains within the cosmic system and closes the sequence mechanically rather than pastorally.
